question: Does an official library record establish a new primary-source lead for Pampanga freshwater research, and is it independent from the 2009 Silliman Journal article?

catalogSearch.query: Survey of indigenous and introduced species in the freshwater ecosystems in Pampanga

verifiedBibliographicMetadata.author: Romero, Maria Angelee V.
verifiedBibliographicMetadata.titleAsCataloged: Survey of indigenous and introduced species in the freshwater ecosystems in Pampanga
verifiedBibliographicMetadata.nationalLibraryBibliographyEntry: The National Library of the Philippines 2024 Special Bibliography on Indigenous Peoples lists the same author/title/year, xvii, 109 leaves, and M.Sc. Environmental Management thesis designation.
verifiedBibliographicMetadata.institutionLimit: The direct eLib record does not name the degree-granting institution. A secondary 2018 reference attributes the thesis to Central Luzon State University; that attribution is not independently confirmed by the catalog record.

accessAssessment.digitalCopy: Not Available, as stated in the eLib record.
accessAssessment.physicalHolding: The catalog lists the National Library of the Philippines, Filipiniana General Book Theses collection, Manila, with call number 591.76095991 R664s 2006.
accessAssessment.clsuOpac: The official CLSU library site links to an OPAC, but the OPAC target timed out during this review; no title-level CLSU catalog result was obtained.
accessAssessment.outreach: No author, library, government office, or institution was contacted. No access control was bypassed.

lineageAssessment.possibleRelationship: The 2006 thesis is by Maria Angelee V. Romero, who is also a co-author of the 2009 Silliman Journal article on freshwater ecosystems in Nueva Ecija and Pampanga. The 2009 article reports Pampanga sampling in Candaba Swamp and Pampanga River reaches at Apalit, San Simon, and San Luis.
lineageAssessment.evidenceForIdentity: Author, topic, province, and chronology overlap, making the thesis a plausible source or precursor for the 2009 Pampanga section.
lineageAssessment.unresolved: The thesis text, field dates, station names, sample records, and a thesis-to-article statement were not available. It is not established whether the article reuses, expands, summarizes, or independently repeats thesis sampling.
lineageAssessment.decision: Treat the thesis and article as related source leads, not independent evidence. Do not add their taxa or sample totals together. The 2006 NAST proceedings abstract is a separate Nueva Ecija-only source and does not resolve the Pampanga thesis lineage.

rightsAssessment.thesisReuseTerms: Not reviewed because the thesis content was unavailable.
rightsAssessment.decision: Retain bibliographic metadata and the access/lineage lead for internal research only. Do not reproduce thesis content or publish derived checklist rows without reviewing the primary text and its applicable rights.

nextActions: Keep the thesis as a retrieval and lineage lead; if a lawful copy becomes available, compare its field dates, stations, methods, fish tables, and acknowledgments against the 2009 Silliman article before treating any evidence as independent.
Continue Central Luzon freshwater and brackish research with independently attributable sources and keep Pampanga, Central Luzon, and Luzon incomplete.
